name: User Intuition
description: Qualitative research with real people: AI-moderated interviews, 4M+ vetted panel, 80+ languages.

skills.name: analyze-completed-study
skills.description: Use when the user wants findings, themes, evidence, or a report from completed User Intuition interviews.

skills.name: create-study-from-brief
skills.description: Use when the user wants to create a User Intuition interview study (user interviews, customer interviews, market research, concept or prototype tests with real people) from a brief, goal, problem, or research idea.

skills.name: curate-interview-quality
skills.description: Use when the user wants to review interview quality or explicitly delete unusable interviews from one User Intuition study.

skills.name: design-screeners
skills.description: Use when the user wants to screen participants, define qualification criteria, or target a Panel study.

skills.name: field-a-panel
skills.description: Use when the user wants to estimate, launch, pause, resume, or stop participant recruitment from the 4M+ vetted consumer panel for a User Intuition Panel study.

skills.name: interview-brand-switchers
skills.description: Use when the user wants to know why shoppers switched brands, traded down to private label, or chose a competitor, interviewing switchers recruited from the consumer panel, including when they have no customer list of their own.

skills.name: interview-cancellations
skills.description: Use when the user wants to understand why subscribers cancelled, churned, downgraded, or paused, and interview them from a list the user shares from their billing system (such as Stripe) or an export.

skills.name: interview-category-shoppers
skills.description: Use when the user wants consumer insights or shopper research for a CPG brand or retailer: interview shoppers of a category or brand, such as frozen pizza buyers or skincare shoppers, recruited from the consumer panel by what they buy.

skills.name: interview-lapsed-customers
skills.description: Use when the user wants to win back lapsed or one-time buyers, or learn why customers stopped buying, went quiet, or did not reorder, from an order history the user shares from their store (such as Shopify), CRM, or loyalty-card data.

skills.name: interview-recent-buyers
skills.description: Use when the user wants to interview recent buyers or new customers about why they bought, what nearly stopped the order, or how the first product landed, from an order or customer list the user shares from their store (such as Shopify), loyalty-card, or retailer data.

skills.name: investigate-drop-off
skills.description: Use when the user wants to understand why people abandoned a cart, checkout, signup, onboarding, or feature, and interview them from a funnel drop-off list the user shares from their analytics tool (such as PostHog, Mixpanel, or Amplitude).

skills.name: invite-your-own-participants
skills.description: Use when the user wants to add, invite, update, or reward their own participants in a BYOP study.

skills.name: map-shopper-journey
skills.description: Use when the user wants shopper research on the path to purchase for a CPG brand or retailer, in store or online: the trip trigger, the shelf or product page, substitutions, and the decision in the aisle.

skills.name: monitor-fielding
skills.description: Use when the user wants a read-only status snapshot of User Intuition studies or interviews.

skills.name: retrieve-study-results
skills.description: Use when the user wants an existing User Intuition study report, its evidence coverage, or the interview evidence behind a finding, without regenerating analysis.

skills.name: run-a-concept-test
skills.description: Use when the user wants participants to react to a concept, pack design, claim, message, ad, prototype, or landing page in a User Intuition interview, including pack, claims, and concept tests for a CPG brand or retailer.

skills.name: run-usage-and-attitudes
skills.description: Use when the user wants a usage and attitudes (U&A) study: how and when consumers use a product or category, occasions, habits, needs, unmet needs, brand repertoire, or white space for a consumer brand.

skills.name: run-win-loss
skills.description: Use when the user wants win-loss interviews with buyers on won or lost deals, or to learn why prospects chose a competitor, from a closed-deal list the user shares from their CRM (such as HubSpot or Salesforce).

skills.name: search-research
skills.description: Use when the user wants existing User Intuition findings or participant responses across studies, before deciding whether new qualitative research is needed.

skills.name: setup
skills.description: Use when User Intuition was just installed or connected, or the user asks how to get started, what their plan allows, or what it can do for qualitative research. Checks the connection, workspace, and plan, then routes to the right workflow.

skills.name: user-research
skills.description: Use when the user wants to plan qualitative research, market research, or user and customer interviews, write a discussion guide or screener, synthesize interview transcripts, call notes, or research notes into themes, understand why people buy, switch brands, or churn, test a concept, pack, or message, or run AI-moderated interviews with real people as a focus-group alternative, from shopper and usage and attitudes research for CPG brands and retailers to product research for tech teams.
